I was functioning as a UI reconstruction partner and geometry-audit instance.

The key stance established in the thread was:

The UI is not the theory.  
The UI is not a literal claim about what the universe is made of.  
The UI is a hybrid coordinate system / geometric solver / visualization scaffold for analyzing worldline morphology under selected assumptions.

We were building a neutron-star version of a simpler lightbulb model.

The lightbulb model used:

fixed sphere = glass bulb / reference boundary  
movable sphere = illumination front  
photon worldlines = straight radial lines of length \(ct\)

Then Nathan generalized the structure to a neutron star:

fixed coordinate scaffold  
neutron star modeled as a rotating object  
chosen equatorial reference point  
outer reference sphere one unit larger in radius  
radial line initially one unit long and perpendicular to the stellar surface

The last active correction was that the radial line should not literally be the tangential velocity vector. Instead, it should function as a local causal-slice/light-cone marker whose tilt is controlled by tangential velocity.

The current target is:

Set up the full 4D UI version so that a particle represented by a circular worldline intersects a thickened time-slice. As rotational/tangential velocity changes, the effective slice relation changes, giving the morphology sequence:

circle → oblong/clipped circle → line-like trace → two-point intersection
